dedupe_keys.name: gmed global manufacturing employment database 126 countries 1950s 2022

description: GMED gives the share of employment in manufacturing for 126 countries from the 1950s to 2022, to study the weight of manufacturing and deindustrialisation over time. The Mendeley Data record says it combines the ILOSTAT database and the GGDC 10-sector database (2014 release) into 4,810 observations, 5 to 75 per country (average 38), with about 30 percent European economies, 20 percent Asian, 20 percent Latin American and 15 percent African, the rest being China, North America, Australia and New Zealand and island and other economies. Version 2 (September 2024) by Erika Majzlíková has 2023 and 2024 releases as Excel and Stata files with introductions in PDF and the source extracts, about 2.8 MB in total, free to download under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is global. Caveats: series are unbalanced, and joining two sources can create breaks. For simulation it gives how much of each country's workforce depends on factories, a reference layer for the social impact of industrial disruptions. Related catalogue records include the NBER-CES Manufacturing Industry Database and the UNIDO INDSTAT data at the UK Data Service.
